title: The Water Drop Experiment
text: “Well, in any case, if there’s an underwater gimmick, Ren and I will go check it out.”

And so, the pairing for when we needed to venture underwater was decided, I say. We continued advancing steadily down the path. Naturally, we encountered monsters along the way as well. As expected, a boss appeared before the next floor. All Karma-type bosses, indeed. Once we’d pushed on to the next floor, Father brought up another topic.
“About that chat earlier—honestly, out of everyone’s worlds, the one I’d most want to visit is Ren’s. I really want to try a VR game.”
“You’re that curious about my world?”
“Well… I suppose I am curious too, now that you mention it. Based on that earlier guess, it sounds like you could even fly freely through the sky.”
“Itsuki, you can already fly freely through the sky, can’t you?”
Via reverse-thrust flight, I say.
“Please don’t bring back the thing I was trying to forget.”
“You’re the one who said it sounded like you could fly through the sky.”
“Self-inflicted wound, that. Careless of him, indeed.”
Itsuki, prone to careless slips of the tongue, was quite the airhead in general, I say. Truly fitting, being Rafuemon’s owner. No wonder Filoko-chan laughed.
“That’s not what I meant—I mean flying while ignoring gravity, don’t you think?”
“Well… there are certainly zones where you can move freely through the air, ignoring gravity…”
“There are…”
“If you stumble into a poorly-adjusted zone, you’ll suddenly plummet from a great height and get quite a shock.”
“Waah… that sounds scary, like a roller coaster. Though I guess it wouldn’t actually hurt even if you slammed into the ground?”

“Apparently there was no tactile sensation in the early days, but by the time Brave Star Online came out, they’d managed to reproduce quite a lot of it. Though I heard they had to dial back the precision, since if there’s too little difference from reality, your brain might end up killing your body.”
“Naofumi-san, do you understand the concern Ren-san is explaining?”
“Some kind of disorder caused by belief, maybe? I’ve heard that if an experience is too realistic, the body ends up reflecting what the mind believes.”

“The opposite of the placebo effect, where something that isn’t medicine produces an effect because you believe it is—the nocebo effect, I say. A phenomenon where side effects occur even though there shouldn’t be any.”
“Motoyasu-san, you really do have some odd bits of knowledge. Though speaking of being prone to strong beliefs, you’re practically the poster child for it.”
“Shh! He’ll hear you.”
I heard that loud and clear, Itsuki! Though I can’t deny that this particular bit of knowledge came courtesy of some science-minded pig, indeed.
“In my world, there’s an urban legend I’m still not sure is real or not, called the Bouamed Water Drop Experiment, I say.”
“Huh, so that’s the name. I couldn’t quite recall it myself.”

“To summarize: after explaining to a death row inmate the amount of blood loss required to bleed to death, they blindfolded him and bound him, made small cuts on his hands and feet with a scalpel—though no actual wound was made—and kept dripping water to make him believe blood was dripping from those spots. Then, right when they declared the lethal amount had been reached, the condemned man died, or so the story goes, I say.”
A tale I confirmed for myself later, after hearing a pig speak of it, I say.
“By definition, it’s said to be death by curse in a certain world of Japan, distinct from the curses of this world, indeed.”
“So it’s about the mechanism of ‘cursing’ in modern society. The idea that believing you’re cursed by someone causes your health to deteriorate.”
“I’ve heard of murders caused by hypnosis-type supernatural abilities, so something similar exists in my world too. I see… that does explain why certain ability users get called ‘curse-type.’”
“So even VR gets scary once it’s too realistic, huh.”

“Getting that immersed is a bit much in itself. Though even with reduced precision, there are people with an acquired constitution who feel the in-game sensations especially strongly—and those types tend to be strong in games, but…”
At that, Ren turned his gaze toward Father, though it seemed less like he was looking at Father and more like he was looking through him at something else entirely, indeed.
“Father, what about my world?”
“Motoyasu-kun himself has zero desire to go back, plus it’s a world without Filolials, so I doubt he’d go. And like I said before, I’d probably just end up as some background extra there.”
I have absolutely no desire to return, I say. And just then, a sharp pain shot through my head once again.

『Oh dear. I suppose I feel a bit sorry for you—or something like that… After your lifespan ends, you’ll be sent back to spin the wheel of parallel branches in your original world, Japan, again… I suppose that’s just the way of your world, but it does sound rough.』
『Well, the laws of each world differ, after all. It seems the spirit of the spear pulled you out while saving you from death, but…』

『Reading the mastermind’s method, it looks like they killed off the other candidates so the first choice couldn’t be summoned. A method that exploits the spirit’s nature—its inability to overlook a death right in front of it.』
“Motoyasu-kun?”
Father tilted his head slightly and called out to me. That voice… but for now, answering Father took priority.
“Right. I have not the slightest intention of returning, I say.”
I’d already told Father before that I felt not a shred of lingering attachment to my original world. Still, if Father was curious, then I, Motoyasu, would gladly explain all manner of things to him.
“See? Even Ren and Itsuki probably wouldn’t want my world or Motoyasu-kun’s world, since they’re too old-fashioned for their taste.”
“I do think there’s a certain charm to the retro feel, but… it does seem like it’d cause plenty of trouble.”
“It’s true the era is a bit different, certainly.”
“Naofumi, what about Itsuki’s world?”
“It’s a world where supernatural abilities are basically human rights, right? Wouldn’t that be rough for me? Ah, but if I could use the powers from this world as-is, that might actually be fun.”
So the idea would be storming into Itsuki’s world using powers from this one, indeed.
“Supernatural powers are nothing to fear, I say.”

“Naofumi-san, you’re already highly suspected of being some kind of esper yourself, so it probably wouldn’t matter whether you could use this world’s powers or not. And given the chance you might have multiple abilities, I’d honestly rather you didn’t come.”
“Itsuki, don’t you want to go back to your original world?”
At Father’s question, Itsuki threw both hands up as if to say absolutely not.
“If I went to Itsuki’s world, though…”
Ren seemed to be imagining it as well.
“Even more unremarkable than Naofumi or Motoyasu. Especially with no magic and no weapons.”
“Calling yourself more unremarkable than me feels like way too much self-deprecation, though…”
“If you went to a school unrelated to supernatural powers, I think you could live a normal life. Though admittedly, it’d be utterly without excitement.”
“If anything, it’s strange that Naofumi seems like he could adapt to either world.”
Ren muttered this, and Itsuki let out a sigh. Which just goes to show how capable Father truly is, I say.
“Adapting, sure, but… I’d only want to try VR games in Ren’s world—adapting enough to actually live there is a whole different story, isn’t it?”
“You could just get a part-time job at some restaurant somewhere and that alone would cover living expenses, and if you bought VR gear you’d probably do decently well in-game.”
“I’m not as skilled with a sword as you, Ren. My little brother did kendo, though.”
“I wonder about that… Naofumi, you’re good at dressing monsters, and you can spot the vital points at a glance, can’t you?”
“You can do that too, can’t you, Ren? Whether it’s people or monsters, the structure of a living body is more or less similar across the board.”
I could tell too, indeed. One good hit to the head or heart does the job.

“I have a feeling that if Naofumi weren’t the Shield Hero, he’d land a fatal blow on the first try even without any swordsmanship training. Like, if some higher-level monster opened its jaws and lunged with its claws, he’d instantly jam a sword straight down its throat and finish it off.”
“What kind of acrobatic attack is that? You’re giving me way too much credit.”
“After seeing that knife work of his, I can’t exactly deny it. Wouldn’t be surprising if he drained the blood mid-air, then neatly stripped the fur off and turned it straight into meat.”

Even Itsuki was piling on after Ren’s comment now, indeed. It’s true, Father’s mid-air cooking skills are impressive. So it wouldn’t be strange at all if he could pull that off, I say. And here, I suddenly recalled the time Kou made Father angry. Ironically, that Father was this very same Father, indeed. He’d skillfully marked dotted lines all over Kou’s bound body, properly labeling the location of each organ.
“Somehow Motoyasu-san, despite being in his Usauni form, is striking some sort of pose straight out of a horror picture.”
“What’s he doing? I’m guessing he’s imagining something odd and scaring himself over his own delusions, but…”
“Maybe he’s remembering a yandere? What with the knife connection and all.”

“Who knows, honestly. Probably something Filolial-related, though—oh, right, come to think of it, Naofumi-san drew the vital points all over Kou-san’s body with charcoal the very first time they met, didn’t he?”
Guh… Itsuki, damn you! Landing a direct hit on my imagination at a time like this.
